gaps.sentence: The mixture will ___ as it cools (SOLID).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ify forms the verb: solidify means to become solid. A base verb follows 'will'.

gaps.sentence: After the long journey, we were all ___ (EXHAUST).
gaps.explanation: People who experience the feeling take -ed: we were exhausted. The journey was exhausting.

gaps.sentence: We had no ___ (CHOOSE) but to cancel the trip.
gaps.explanation: 'Have no choice but to do something' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'choose' is an irregular 'choice'.

gaps.sentence: Her kindness and ___ (GENEROUS) made her very popular.
gaps.explanation: Parallel to 'kindness', a noun is needed: generosity (note the irregular -osity spelling).

gaps.hint: subject of the sentence: noun needed (-ness becomes -ty here)
gaps.explanation: The subject must be a noun: Honesty. The spelling changes -ness to -ty; 'honestness' is not a word.

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: He is under a lot of ___ at work (PRESS).
gaps.hint: noun needed after 'a lot of'; fixed phrase 'under ___'
gaps.explanation: 'Under pressure' is the fixed phrase; the noun of 'press' is 'pressure'.
